metaData.title: Cook Sends Siri Off on Its Final Journey
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: On the eve of WWDC26, this article compiles leaked information to provide a comprehensive preview of Apple's AI strategy 'make-up exam' results: Siri's transformation into an AI companion, a proprietary search engine, AI photo editing, and an open platform, while also exploring the final legacy test of Cook's tenure.
metaData.summary: Published just before Apple's WWDC26, this article, based on leaks from Mark Gurman and others, systematically outlines a comprehensive upgrade to Apple's AI strategy. Core elements include: Siri evolving from a voice command tool into an 'AI companion' with a new Dynamic Island entry point, a standalone app, multi-command processing capabilities, and a foundation built on the Gemini model; Apple's first proprietary web search product, rivaling Perplexity; deep AI integration into the Camera and Photos apps, including Visual Intelligence, AI expansion, and recomposition; and the introduction of the CoreAI system, opening AI capabilities to third parties, potentially creating a new 'agent commission' model. The article concludes by focusing on Cook's tenure, labeling Apple Intelligence a 'major stain' and his last chance before handing over the reins, while analyzing real-world challenges like privacy, hardware costs, and the developer ecosystem.

mainPoints.point: Siri will be completely revamped as an 'AI companion', featuring a Dynamic Island entry point and a standalone app.
mainPoints.explanation: The new Siri supports multi-command processing, text and voice interaction, uses the Gemini model as its foundation, and debuts a standalone chat app, directly competing with ChatGPT.

mainPoints.point: Apple is launching its first proprietary web search product, built into Siri.
mainPoints.explanation: This search capability rivals Perplexity AI, answering user questions in formats like summaries and lists, reducing reliance on Google and ChatGPT.

mainPoints.point: iOS 27 will deeply revamp the Camera and Photos apps, introducing AI expansion and recomposition.
mainPoints.explanation: Visual Intelligence features are integrated into the Camera app, adding nutrition label recognition; photo editing gains AI expansion (generating out-of-frame content) and spatial photo recomposition tools.

mainPoints.point: Apple is opening AI capabilities to third parties through the CoreAI system, potentially enabling a new commission model.
mainPoints.explanation: Developers can integrate with Siri and Apple's AI services, and third-party AI models (like Claude, Gemini) can be offered via the App Store, with analysts suggesting Apple could become an 'agent call market'.

mainPoints.point: Apple Intelligence is a 'stain' on Cook's tenure and his last chance before handing over the reins.
mainPoints.explanation: The article cites analysts who argue Siri must evolve from a passive command portal into a cross-app agent to justify its valuation, but faces real challenges including a developer ecosystem 'chicken-and-egg' dilemma, privacy constraints, and hardware costs.

keyQuotes: Apple has no more excuses not to deliver results.
Apple Intelligence is 'a major stain' on Cook's tenure and 'his last chance to spark an AI inflection point before John Ternus takes over as CEO'.
A truly intelligent Siri could easily erect new paywalls in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: Why Did Hermes Take Over from OpenClaw in Just Two Months?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth comparison between the rising open-source AI Agent star Hermes and its predecessor OpenClaw, arguing that Hermes' success stems not from functional superiority but from encapsulating decision complexity—such as skill auto-evolution and proactive memory management—within underlying deterministic rules. This engineering safety net allowed it to deliver an automated 'gets better with use' experience precisely when the underlying technology was just barely sufficient.

relatedArticles.title: A Serious Discussion: How Much of Our Skills Can Skill Actually Distill? | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the capability boundaries of AI Agent Skills, pointing out that while they excel at encoding explicit rules and knowledge routing, they cannot capture the tacit intuition and utility judgment that human experts rely on in complex decision-making.

relatedArticles.title: iPhone Finally Gets Siri AI! But Mainland China Misses Out on the First Release, Alarm Clock Becomes the Biggest Surprise
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: WWDC26 unveils iOS 27 and new Apple Intelligence developments, upgrading Siri to a system-level AI assistant with its own app, but users in mainland China will temporarily miss out on the AI features.

relatedArticles.title: Tech Enthusiast Weekly (Issue 399): Notes on Visiting China's AI Giants
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article excerpts the impressions of a US tech analyst after visiting 14 Chinese AI companies, covering 11 dimensions including computing power gap, computational efficiency, open-source divergence, talent structure, and attitudes toward AI safety, presenting a realistic view of China's AI industry.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Microsoft Build 2026: The 'Agent-First' Era Arrives with Seven In-House Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Microsoft Build 2026 unveiled seven in-house MAI models, the Scout agent, the MXC system-level security sandbox, and Project Solara, marking the full implementation of an 'Agent-First' strategy.

relatedArticles.title: Dowson Tong and Yao Shunyu in Conversation: Tencent AI's Second Half
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Dowson Tong, Senior Executive Vice President of Tencent Group, and Yao Shunyu, Chief AI Scientist, engaged in a joint dialogue centered on the core propositions of AI's second half—shifting from 'solving problems' to 'defining problems,' Co-Design of models and products, the evolution and cost-effectiveness of Agent technology, and Tencent's strategic pace and organizational transformation in the AI era—offering a deep conversation blending strategic vision with engineering practice.

relatedArticles.title: Kimi Work Beta Invitation: Let Us Share Your Workload
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Kimi launches the beta version of 'Kimi Work', a general-purpose local Agent for knowledge workers, migrating Coding Agent capabilities to a desktop GUI, supporting natural language-driven complex task decomposition, multi-Agent parallel collaboration, and tool invocation.

relatedArticles.title: In the AI-Induced Cognitive Disarmament, We Will Lose More Than Just Ability | Hao Chat on Trends
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: From the perspectives of cognitive psychology, labor sociology, and philosophy, this article systematically argues that the 'cognitive disarmament' brought about by AI is not a simple degradation of abilities, but a historic turning point where alienation has deepened from the labor process to the thought generation process, rooted in the growth society's endless pursuit of efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Q1 2026: AI Agents Come of Age | 2026 Q1 AI Trend White Paper
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of four structural trends in AI Agents for Q1 2026: long-horizon productization, harness engineering, recursive R&D, and the Skill ecosystem, revealing the flywheel effect as Agents evolve from tools into independent 'new colleagues'.
